title: Dodgers' Dave Roberts Announces Shohei Ohtani Update After Leaving Rockies Game - NewsBreak
text: Two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani didn't miss a beat in his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers last year, but this year is a different animal. In addition to being an elite hitter, the three-time MVP is now back on the mound after not pitching in 2024 due to his UCL injury. Ohtani is still earning the majority of his money at the plate, as he entered Wednesday's bout with the Colorado Rockies slashing .284/.392/.623 with 44 homers and 83 RBI over 124 games. Meanwhile, the 31-year-old also had a 3.47 ERA in just nine starts. However, if Ohtani notches close to his 3.03 career ERA in this year's playoffs, it'll add another element to a Los Angeles squad that won the 2024 World Series without him pitching. That's why the team needs him even more than most squads need their superstars. Unfortunately for the Dodgers, though, Ohtani took a line drive off his leg in the fourth inning while he was pitching on Wednesday. The five-time All-Star completed the frame before converting to designated hitter in the fifth. Backup outfielder Alex Call then pinch-hit for him in the eighth. Los Angeles provided an update about Ohtani postgame, via NBC LA's Michael J. Duarte. Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images "Dave Roberts said the 94 MPH comebacker hit Shohei Ohtani 'square in the thigh,'" he reported. "He expected it to tighten up on him. He’s got a scheduled day off tomorrow to get more treatment on it." Ohtani finished 1-for-2 with one walk and allowed five runs in four innings, picking up his first loss of the season. The Rockies won 8-3 and have won two of three contests in the series thus far. The Dodgers are now in danger of losing a series to one of the worst teams ever. Colorado is 37-90 (.291 winning percentage) and needs several more wins to avoid the top-10 worst single-season records in the modern era (1901-present). The 1942 Philadelphia Phillies had the 10th-worst record by winning percentage at 42-109 (.278). Southpaw pitcher Clayton Kershaw will start for Los Angeles on Thursday night against Colorado right-hander Chase Dollander.
